title: What is known about 1RB1LC_1LA0RD_1LB1LF_1LE1RE_0LA0RB_0LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_1LA0RD_1LB1LF_1LE1RE_0LA0RB_0LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The left side is two big blocks of ones (at 109 steps B>0 1^37710 0 1^7702 0 1^138); every cycle moves 18 cells out of one and 24 into the other, so the regimes grow by 4/3. Lean proves the 40 cycle rules used on the run to 1015 steps; the accelerated run reaches 1040 steps without a halt. Its regime lengths follow the same pattern as those of 1RB1LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_1RC0LA_1RD1RF_0RD---.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 45,954 cells have been visited and 45,454 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072).

claims.title: The cycle rules
claims.text: 40 one-cycle rules, each for all values of its variables, e.g. (111)^n2 +8 and (111)^n4 −6 per cycle: the rules the cycle accelerator applied on the run to 1015 steps.

claims.title: No halt up to 10<sup>40</sup> steps
claims.text: bbtools.cycles with blocks of 3 cells: 146 jumps, 78 proved rules, no halt by 1040 steps.

claims.title: The 4/3 map
claims.text: Cycles per regime: 3, 7, 10, 14, 18, 23, …, 75496, 100978, 134640, 179519, 239361, 319153, 425537, 567383, 756508, 1008656, 1344830, 1793083, 2390779, 3187809, 4250412, 5667216: each about 4/3 of the last. The small blocks that come and go at the end of the tape (111^13, 111^24, 111^45, 111^192, 111^459, 111^597, …) are the same numbers as in the run of 1RB1LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_1RC0LA_1RD1RF_0RD---, which suggests the two machines simulate the same map.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open: the end-of-regime rule is not extracted, so the halting transition (F reading 1) is not reduced to a condition on the map.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Two big blocks of ones trade cells, four in for every three out, so each round is a third longer than the one before: a Collatz-like map that looks like a twin of another holdout.

facts.text: No halt in the accelerated (proved-rule) run.
Cycle rules of the run to 10<sup>15</sup>, proved in Lean.
Each regime about 4/3 as long as the last.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072).
After 109 steps the tape spans 45,954 cells (33,936 left of the start, 77 right), with a density of 1s of 0.989.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Two big blocks of ones
html: After 109 steps the left side is B>0 1^37710 0 1^7702 0 1^138, and about 15 million steps later B>0 1^37080 0 1^8542 0 1^138: the outer block lost 630 cells and the inner gained 840, four for every three. Right of the start there are only 77 cells, a slow counter.

sections.heading: Four in, three out
html: Read in blocks of 3 cells, one cycle adds 8 words 111 to one block and removes 6 from the other (proved, for every size). When the shrinking block is used up a new regime starts, about 4/3 as long: the cycles per regime go 3, 7, 10, 14, 18, 23, …, 1344830, 1793083, 2390779, 3187809, 4250412.

The small blocks that appear at the end of the tape between regimes (13, 24, 45, 192, 459, 597 words …) are exactly the ones seen in 1RB1LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_1RC0LA_1RD1RF_0RD---, another holdout of the same shape: the two machines seem to compute the same map.

sections.heading: Open
html: The only halting transition is F reading 1. As for its twin, the end-of-regime map (how the remainder mod 3 changes the short tail) has not been extracted, so the question is not yet reduced. The accelerated run reaches 1040 steps without a halt.

summary: Two long blocks of ones left of the start trade cells, 8 three-cell words in for every 6 out per cycle, so each regime is about 4/3 as long as the last: a Collatz-like 4n/3 map with a short tail of small blocks; halting not reduced yet.
